newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank shares fall on renewed selling demand.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank shares fall on renewed selling demand.

text.p: Shares in Japan's banking sector fell in Tokyo on Friday on renewed selling interest after the market had confirmed their upward limits.

As of 0521 GMT, shares in Nippon Credit Bank Ltd were down 2 yen to 238 yen with a turnover of 7.26 million, the second-largest volume on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE). Sumitomo Bank Ltd dropped 40 yen to 1,540 yen with a turnover of 2.64 million.
Brokers said market sentiment remained bearish towards the banking sector, which is saddled with massive bad loans, but that no hectic sell-off had been detected so far on Friday.

"Despite the selling in some city banks, the movement in shares in banks such as Nippon Credit and Hokkaido Takushoku is relatively small, so it may not be a sell-off as seen in the past," one broker said.
